segments: The Chronography of Bar Hebraeus.
and they were receiving with them the force of the rams' heads.
They also laid timbers in the trench and covered them with earth by night,
so that the Persians might not see.
And when about five hundred armed Persians approached,
and set timbers {OCR: ܓܝܣܐ / ܩܝܣܐ} against the wall to climb up,
and covered the bridges with bull-hides,
and made a large structure/mound {kudantā} and a path for going up,
the people within poured the water of boiled fenugreek together with oil onto the structure,
and made it slippery.
And they secretly set fire in the timbers underneath the structure.
And when they were hindered for about six hours from entering through these slippery places,
the fire flared up from beneath,
and the structure fell,
and the Persians fell and were crushed and burned.
And the king was ashamed,
especially by the wicked insults that the insiders cast at him.
And he asked of the citizens
that they give him a little silver and he would depart.
Indeed, if they had spoken a good word to him, he would have departed.
They, however, answered most foolishly:
"It is ours to demand of you the price of the vegetables and grass that you have consumed!"
He, seeing their arrogance, persevered.
And as he said,
on that night Christ appeared to him in a dream and said to him:
"After three days I will deliver the city,
because its inhabitants have become arrogant."
Therefore, in the western sector near Tripologrion {or Tripylon},
was the watch of the monks of the Monastery of John of the Urṭaye.
And opposite this tower outside was encamped a certain marzban, Qanraq the lame,
a crafty man.
Now it happened on one of the nights that there was darkness and heavy rain.
And someone had made a supper for the monks,
and gave them wine to drink,
and they sank into sleep.
Now a certain brawler, a rebel and thief named Quṭrana,
used continually to go out and steal and snatch livestock from the Persians.
And when he went out as usual on that night,
Qanraq noticed him and pursued after him,
and he approached even to the wall near the opening where that Quṭrana was entering and leaving;
and the monks did not cry out,
and he knew that they were asleep.
And the Persians brought ladders and climbed up,
and killed {OCR: ܩܛܓܘ for ܩܛܠܘ} the monks.
And when the governor noticed, he came with... {OCR: illegible/garbled text}.
